orders.instruction: First attempt: probe each keyboard action and compare successive frames to learn movement, obstacles and goal cues online. Track visited state-action pairs; penalize repeated loops and choose unexplored transitions. Use observed progress to select actions and re-probe when the level changes.

First attempt: identify visible components and probe their centers individually. Learn which clicks change the board and how; prioritize responsive components, suppress unchanged clicks, and infer a goal-directed sequence from observed transitions. Re-detect components after each change.

First attempt: probe keyboard actions and component-center clicks separately to learn which controls affect each visible object. Build an online transition map, favor actions that approach observed goal cues, and avoid revisiting failed state-action pairs. Relearn control effects after level transitions.

summary: Fill all 3 slots with untried games across keyboard, click and mixed controls. Require observation-driven learning and loop avoidance; count success only when levels beat every control. Stop scheduling at 85% budget.
